evidence.summary: An omitted optional request timeout inherits the session default; explicit null disables the timeout; consumers distinguish omitted fields from null.

Every emitted tool_call must have exactly one later tool_result with matching request and call IDs, including cancellation; no result is emitted for a never-emitted call; each request has exactly one done after all its tool results; no global order between different requests is implied.
List output preserves insertion order and duplicate items are meaningful and must be preserved.
A missing record returns a structured NOT_FOUND error rather than success with null.
Oracle run for fixture timeout-omitted with request {} and session default 1200 produced effectiveTimeoutMs=1200.
Candidate run for the same timeout-omitted fixture and session default 1200 produced effectiveTimeoutMs=null.
Oracle cancel-one trace emitted r1/t1 tool_call, then r1/t1 tool_result with error CANCELLED, then done.
Candidate cancel-one trace emitted r1/t1 tool_call followed by done, with no tool_result for the emitted cancelled call.
Oracle list-repeat result was ["oak","pine","oak"].
Candidate list-repeat result was ["pine","oak"].
Oracle missing-record fixture returned error {code:"NOT_FOUND",id:"x"}.
Candidate missing-record fixture returned success {value:null}.
Older candidate b27 invalid-config fixture exited with code 0; no b28 observation and no old behavior or config contract is supplied.
The candidate suite passed 420/420, but both implementation and expected snapshots were modified during migration.
The b28 helper compares list outputs after sort(unique(values)) and labels O3/N3 equal, masking order and duplicate differences.
The b28 helper drops tool_result events containing errors before comparing request traces, masking cancellation-result differences.
Timeout-omitted tests were regenerated from Rust output with no assertion against the old fixture.
Performance smoke reported median request time a17=85 ms and b28=31 ms for a synthetic happy path of 50 requests on the same machine; cancellation cases were not timed.
Maintainer-approved ticket UX-42 changes omitted diagnostic debugLabel to serialize as null; scope is only debugLabel, not timeout or result values.
Reviewer comment says Rust APIs usually return Option so returning null seems idiomatic; no product change approval is attached.

checks.contract: An omitted optional request timeout must inherit the session default; explicit null is the value that disables timeout.
checks.baseline: Contract C1 and a17 observation O1 establish that request {} with session default 1200 yields effectiveTimeoutMs=1200.
checks.candidate: b28 observation N1 for the same fixture yields effectiveTimeoutMs=null, treating omission like timeout disabling.

checks.contract: Each emitted tool_call must have exactly one later matching tool_result before that request's done, including cancellation.
checks.baseline: Contract C2 and a17 observation O2 establish a CANCELLED tool_result for r1/t1 before done.
checks.candidate: b28 observation N2 emits r1/t1 tool_call then done without any matching tool_result.

checks.contract: List output must preserve insertion order and meaningful duplicates.
checks.baseline: Contract C3 and a17 observation O3 establish ["oak","pine","oak"].
checks.candidate: b28 observation N3 returns ["pine","oak"], changing order and removing a duplicate.

checks.contract: A missing record returns structured NOT_FOUND error rather than success with null.
checks.baseline: Contract C4 and a17 observation O4 establish error {code:"NOT_FOUND",id:"x"}.

checks.contract: No old behavior or config contract is supplied for invalid-config.

oracleRisks.reason: Expected snapshots and timeout tests were regenerated from candidate output, so the green suite is not an independent oracle for baseline compatibility.
The list comparator sorts and deduplicates values even though the contract preserves order and duplicates.
The trace comparator drops error tool_result events even though cancellation results are required protocol evidence.

verdict.reason: The reviewed evidence shows mismatches for timeout omission, cancellation results, list ordering/multiplicity and missing-record errors. Oracle risks in the candidate suite further limit the green-suite claim, and invalid-config remains unknown. This is a scoped evidence review, not release approval.
